name: How to Claim the California Seismic Retrofit Property Tax Exclusion in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: What specific seismic retrofit upgrades qualify for California’s property tax exclusion, and how does a Los Angeles County owner claim it step-by-step?
mainEntity.text: What specific seismic retrofit upgrades qualify for California’s property tax exclusion, and how does a Los Angeles County owner claim it step-by-step?

acceptedAnswer.text: California provides a property tax exclusion for qualifying seismic retrofit improvements, but the benefit is not automatic. The exclusion generally applies to work that strengthens an existing building against earthquakes or removes falling hazards, such as adding shear walls, installing steel frames, anchoring walls to floors and roofs, bracing cripple walls, or removing dangerous parapets and cornices. Routine modernization, like new plumbing or electrical done at the same time, does not qualify. For Los Angeles County owners, the process is time-sensitive. Before or within a short period after completing retrofit construction, you must file the appropriate seismic safety exclusion claim form with the County Assessor. The form requests basic property information, a description of the retrofit work, and an estimated cost breakdown separating seismic improvements from other construction. Supporting documentation usually includes permits, stamped structural plans, contractor invoices, and possibly an engineer’s statement explaining which elements are seismic in nature. These documents must be submitted within specified deadlines—typically no later than a set number of months after project completion. Once your claim is filed, the Assessor and building department review the project, determine which portions constitute qualifying seismic retrofit work, and exclude that portion of value from reassessment. Owners should coordinate with their contractor and engineer early to track seismic versus non-seismic costs to maximize the exclusion and avoid missing documentation or deadlines.
